status: successful CI artifact independently re-inspected; scanner correction committed, new CI not yet checked

debug.explanation: Rust's unoptimized Wasm contains separate division/remainder but inserts Rust panic branches and rotates into other functions. CLIF shows split basic blocks; the narrow adjacent same-block fusion cannot match them.

optimized.explanation: Optimized LLVM/Rust lowers same-operand remainder to (x - (x / y) * y); CLIF contains one division, imul and isub, with no urem to fuse. Disassembly similarly uses one divq plus imul/sub. Other swapped operand controls are ineligible.

scanner_defect.observation: The earlier emitted-CLIF lexical scanner matched only untyped `udiv`/`urem` and silently skipped the actual `udiv.i64`/`urem.i64` syntax; its earlier zero count was not valid evidence until independently rescanned.

costs.interpretation: Neither profile yielded any baseline-versus-patched emitted-byte or instruction savings. ELF .text is aligned whole-module cost, not individual function native cost.

next_target: Separately evaluate (A) control-flow-aware same-operand div/rem fusion that preserves Rust trap order and dominance, and (B) optimized-CLIF quotient/multiply/subtract remainder reconstruction into the x86 two-result division. First test against a confirmed same-Wasm baseline and verify flags, signed overflow, divide-by-zero and liveness. Avoid broad unproved compiler changes.
limitations: No automatic applicability to typical Rust applications established
